name: Jamie Trimmer
home_bio: My focus is mission and encounter design, with a particular interest in making worlds feel inhabited without relying on dialogue to do the heavy lifting.

projects.title: Red Dead Online
projects.tags: Mission design, encounter design, content at scale
intro: I worked across Red Dead Online from beta through to Blood Money in 2021, contributing to every major role release during that period including Bounty Hunter, Trader, Collector, Moonshiner and Naturalist.

Content was authored using a combination of a visual content creation tool and structured data scripting, a hybrid approach that allowed designers to shape mission flow, pacing and escalation without writing bespoke code. The design challenge throughout was making a fundamentally repeatable structure (go somewhere, get something, bring it back) feel varied, purposeful and worth repeating across hundreds of pieces of content.

projects.title: GTA Online
projects.tags: Mission design, heists and contracts, templating
intro: I worked across GTA Online from The Contract in 2021 through to The Chop Shop in 2023, contributing to five major updates across that period.

Content was authored using a combination of a visual content creation tool and structured data scripting, a hybrid approach that allowed designers to shape mission flow, pacing and escalation without writing bespoke code. The design challenge throughout was keeping missions fresh in a game where players had seen everything and expectations were high.

As with RDO, the team developed a templating approach to deliver content at scale across multiple updates, allowing mission logic and structure to be established once and rapidly adapted across different locations and scenarios.

projects.title: GTA VI
intro: I worked on GTA VI at Rockstar North, designing and implementing content using more complex design and implementation methods, including in-engine visual scripting and C#. That meant adapting quickly to new proprietary tooling and learning C# scripting on the job, and extending and adapting existing gameplay systems to support specific design goals within technical and production constraints.

As one of the earlier members of my team to onboard onto the project, I spent time establishing what worked and what didn't, then passing that knowledge on to colleagues joining later to help speed up their onboarding.

about.title: About me
bio: I’m Jamie, though most people who’ve worked with me know me as JT.

I’ve spent 18 years in the games industry, all of it at Rockstar North, progressing from QA through design support into a full design role. That route gave me a practical, ground-level understanding of how games are actually built, not just designed on paper.

I design missions, encounters and open-world content, and I own the work from early concept through to ship. My QA background means I think about how content breaks as much as how it’s meant to work. Players rarely do what you expect, and I find that interesting rather than frustrating.

I look for unexpected angles. My Paperboy mission ([Acid Lab: Sell](gtao.html#paperboy), on the GTA Online page) is a good example: a delivery brief that became something with its own character because I looked for a different way in. Constraints tend to produce better ideas than open briefs.

Getting content to ship takes constant communication with a lot of people, and I’ve always been more interested in what the team produces together than in protecting individual credit. I also enjoy sharing knowledge: bringing people up to speed and passing on what has and hasn’t worked.

Content that plays identically every time is content players stop noticing, so I build in reasons to come back. In the [Whistleblower](gtao.html#whistleblower) mission (on the GTA Online page), one of three bonus objectives is picked at random, and the improvised cover props left by fleeing workers reward a second look.
I’m based in the Edinburgh area and looking for my next role. Since leaving Rockstar I’ve been building prototypes in Unreal Engine 5 and Godot.
experience: Designed and implemented player-facing open-world gameplay, encounters, and mission content, owning features from early concept through scripting, iteration, and final polish.
Embedded within design teams, supporting gameplay implementation, iteration, and problem-solving across large-scale projects, with increasing ownership and responsibility over time.
Tested gameplay systems and player-facing content on multiple AAA titles, developing a strong foundation in game quality, production realities, and cross-discipline communication.
